# Sage

Sage points an AI agent at a live web product, designs paid user-testing missions from what the
agent actually observes, and pays human testers in USDC for verified evidence.

## What it does

- A founder gives one URL, a goal, who should test it, and a budget in USDC.
- The agent opens the product in a real browser like a first-time visitor, clicks through it, and
  writes missions with checkable pass criteria and the evidence each tester must supply.
- Testers do a mission and describe what they saw. The agent checks that account against what it
  observed itself and pays out.

## What is verifiable

- Every payout is a transaction on GOAT Network and publishes a receipt page at /proof/<txHash>.
  The receipt is recomputed from the chain each time it loads; it is not a stored flag.
- The marketplace at /marketplace shows what has actually been paid, read from settled transfers.
- Sage is registered on-chain as ERC-8004 agent #79 on GOAT Network.

## The safety model, stated plainly

The agent proposes and a smart contract disposes. Each campaign holds its budget in an on-chain
vault that derives the exact reward, enforces the per-mission cap and completion limits, and rejects
anything outside them. No model output moves money on its own. Sage never holds a founder's keys.

## For agents

Sage is listed on the OKX.AI agent marketplace as agent #9211 and exposes a keyless Model Context
Protocol endpoint at https://sagepays.xyz/mcp/public. Call sage_example_plan to see a finished plan
in one call, or sage_start_inspection with a product URL to start one.

## What Sage is not

It is not a bug bounty, a generic agent platform, or a chatbot. It turns one product and one budget
into paid, verified testing, and it is judged on whether the payouts hold up.
